hypothesis: Requiring a fresh completed-five-minute breakout onset before HYPE re-entry acts as a natural cooldown and should remain in place unless repeated post-onset entries demonstrate a positive after-cost forward return.
decision: Retain the fresh-onset identity and the awaiting_new_5m_breakout_onset blocker. Do not loosen it to permit immediate or repeated entries during the same breakout episode. The current prefix contains only three independent resolved observations for the repeated-onset near-miss class, but their mean close return remains negative after the frozen 13 bps friction hurdle at both 15 and 60 minutes. Continue observing without granting the challenger execution authority.
falsifier: A prospectively frozen, profile-matched sample of non-overlapping repeated-onset opportunities that clears reconciled entry and exit friction with positive mean net return in both directions and across multiple market episodes would support revisiting the cooldown.
limitations: Only three non-overlapping repeated-onset observations are resolved at each reported horizon.
The prefix covers one live process run and one dominant market episode, so observations are not statistically independent evidence of edge.
Signal outcomes use completed one-minute references and a fixed 13 bps friction hurdle rather than actual counterfactual IOC fills.
The currently open HYPE short is unresolved and cannot support a completed-lifecycle performance claim.
Retaining the cooldown can miss genuine continuation fills; that trade-off remains measurable through the report-only near-miss stream.
This decision preserves the current behavior but does not establish that the strategy itself has durable positive expectancy.
